title: CRAM · From world model to action
description: Recorded single-robot examples: semantic scenes, spatial questions, transport and navigation. The Siemens laboratory scene is not included yet. All chapters run locally without a robot connection.

chapters.title: A world with meaning
chapters.narration: CRAM knows more than geometry: the semantic digital twin describes objects, handles and usable surfaces. This recorded reference scenario shows a table, milk and two handles.

chapters.title: Making knowledge visible
chapters.narration: The recorded world answers the question about all handles. The answer highlights both handles directly in the 3D scene.

chapters.title: Finding an empty space
chapters.narration: Free areas account for the object dimensions and existing obstacles. The display shows valid positions for the centre of the milk carton. This answer belongs to the recorded world state.
chapters.query: where can I place milk on table?

chapters.title: Executing a semantic task
chapters.narration: Tracy transports the cube to the named table. CRAM resolves the destination during execution and performs grasping, lifting and placement. This is a successful recording with active collision avoidance.

chapters.title: Explaining the plan
chapters.narration: The plan tree breaks transport down into concrete steps. Suitable steps could eventually be replaced by a learned policy. This demonstration does not execute a policy. The tree shows the actions that were actually recorded.

chapters.title: Driving continuously
chapters.narration: A separate PR2 example shows GCS navigation around an obstacle. The base moves continuously, turns toward its direction of travel and keeps collision avoidance active. The different robots belong to separate recorded worlds.
